title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
technique: PagedAttention: block-based non-contiguous KV cache with on-demand allocation, copy-on-write sharing, swap/recompute preemption; vLLM with iteration-level (continuous) batching

optimized_metrics.evidence: In this work, we build vLLM, a high-throughput distributed LLM serving engine on top of PagedAttention
optimized_metrics.locator: §1 (design goal; throughput read off normalized-latency-vs-rate curves, §6.1)

optimized_metrics.evidence: vLLM, an LLM serving system that achieves (1) near-zero waste in KV cache memory and (2) flexible sharing of KV cache within and across requests to further reduce memory usage.
A high-throughput serving system should retain low normalized latency against high request rates.
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: normalized latency of the systems, the mean of every request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length

headline_claim.text: vLLM improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4x with the same level of latency compared to the state-of-the-art systems, such as FasterTransformer and Orca.

reported_metrics.where: §6.2 max sustainable request rate at similar latency (1.7-2.7x vs Orca Oracle)
Fig 2 (waste breakdown), Fig 15 (memory saving from sharing), Fig 13 (avg # batched requests)
Fig 1 right (token/s vs batch size), motivation only

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we measure normalized latency of the systems, the mean of every request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length, as in Orca [60].
metric_definitions.notes: Mean over requests of E2E/output-length (s/token); output length only, not input+output. E2E presumably includes queueing (open-loop Poisson arrivals, latency 'explodes' when queue grows). Not defined further.

metric_definitions.definition_quote: vLLM can sustain 1.7x-2.7x higher request rates compared to Orca (Oracle) and 2.7x-8x compared to Orca (Max), while maintaining similar latencies.
metric_definitions.notes: Throughput is operationalised as the highest request rate before normalized latency blows up (knee of the curve); no explicit SLO value. Fig 1 uses token/s vs batch size.

load_regime: request-rate sweep with Poisson arrivals over synthesized ShareGPT/Alpaca length traces; 1-hour traces (15 min for OPT-175B)
tradeoff_acknowledged: Kernel-level: PagedAttention adds 20-26% higher attention kernel latency vs FasterTransformer kernel (but better end-to-end); block size trade-off between fragmentation and kernel efficiency; swap vs recompute overheads.
hardware: Google Cloud A2 instances, NVIDIA A100 40GB (1-8 GPUs)
workloads: ShareGPT, Alpaca (lengths only), Poisson arrivals; parallel sampling, beam search, shared prefix, chatbot
extractor_notes: Headline throughput is never measured as tokens/s or req/s directly; it is read off normalized-latency-vs-request-rate curves. No tail percentile, no TTFT/TPOT, no SLO. The 'same level of latency' constraint is mean normalized latency.
load_class_quote: we generate request arrival times using Poisson distribution with different request rates (§6.1); 1-hour traces
